# Report Summary

**How does microhabitat and rain affect the transpiration of coast live oak seedlings?**

[Alternative hypothesis]{.underline}: The mean transpiration of oak seedlings among different microhabitats or before and after a rain event does differ and there is an interaction between microhabitat and occurrence of rain.

[Null hypothesis]{.underline}:  The mean transpiration of oak seedlings among different microhabitats or before and after a rain event does not differ and there is no interaction between microhabitat and occurrence of rain.

Transpiration \~ microhabitat \* rain

## Importing Data

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
Height_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Seedling Heights")

Moist_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Soil Moisture")

SPAD_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "SPAD", 
             na = "NA")

licor_wrong <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",
             sheet = "LICOR")

licor_wrong <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore")
```

## Importing LICOR objects

```{r}
LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",              
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> #if we have two cells, put in #same name paste
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

LICOR_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",  
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES,
             col_types = "text")


ALL_Licor_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

ALL_Licor <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = ALL_Licor_NAMES, 
             col_types = "text")

LICOR_Data_Raw <- full_join(LICOR_Data_Raw, ALL_Licor)
```

## Data Cleaning

```{r}
licor_wanted <- LICOR_Data_Raw |> 
  select(SYS_Date_YYYYMMDD, `PORO_E_apparent_mmol+1m-2s-1`, Treatment_NA_NA, `USERDEF_Block Number_NA`, `USERDEF_Tag Number_NA`) #selecting for #date, transpiration, and treatment #colomns

glimpse(licor_wanted) #all variables are characters

levels(licor_wanted$Treatment_NA_NA) #null value, want to see each level of treatment


#fixing levels = null values bc treatment is character, not a factor
licor_wanted_clean <- licor_wanted |>  
  mutate(treatment = (as.factor(Treatment_NA_NA))) |> #switching to factor from character to #see levels
  select(treatment, SYS_Date_YYYYMMDD, `PORO_E_apparent_mmol+1m-2s-1`, `USERDEF_Block Number_NA`, `USERDEF_Tag Number_NA`) |> #remove old date #colomn
  rename(date = SYS_Date_YYYYMMDD, transpiration = `PORO_E_apparent_mmol+1m-2s-1`, Block = `USERDEF_Block Number_NA`, tag_number = `USERDEF_Tag Number_NA`) #rename #colomns to simpler #names


#changing transpiration colomn to numeric
licor_wanted_clean$transpiration <- as.numeric(licor_wanted_clean$transpiration)

licor_wanted_clean <- licor_wanted_clean |> 
  group_by(tag_number) |> 
  mutate(mean_transp = mean(transpiration)) |>  #mean transpiration colomn added to df
  select(!transpiration) |> 
  unique() |> 
  drop_na() #removing na rows


levels(licor_wanted_clean$treatment) #levels are ??, AC, DT, NR, OS


#Removing unnecessary data
licor_wanted_clean |> 
  filter(treatment != "??") #removing ?? data 
```

```{r}
#selecting for colomns with volumetric water content and date
moist_wanted <- Moist_Data_Raw |>
  select(VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc, Treatment, Date, Block)

levels(moist_wanted$Treatment) #null values

#changing character variable trtment as factor to see levels of trtment
moist_wanted <- moist_wanted |> 
  mutate(treatment = (as.factor(Treatment))) |> 
  select(treatment, Date, VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc, Block) |> #removing old treatment #colomn
  rename(date = Date) #rename date to match with licor table

levels(moist_wanted$treatment) #4 levels, AC, DT, NR, OS

moist_transp_table <- full_join(moist_wanted, licor_wanted_clean) #x date is datetimeUTC and y date #is character

#fixing y table date character variable, changing to datetime UTC
licor_wanted_clean$date <-  
  as.Date(licor_wanted_clean$date, format = "%Y-%m-%d", tz = "UTC")

moist_transp_table <- full_join(moist_wanted, licor_wanted_clean) #running code again


#removing "NA" values  
moist_transp_table <- moist_transp_table |>  
  filter(VWC2_perc != "NA", VWC3_perc != "NA")  


#dropping rest of NAs, should now only have complete soil moisture data and transpiration data
moist_transp_table <- moist_transp_table |>  
  drop_na()

#creating colomn with mean soil moisture
moist_transp_table <- moist_transp_table |> 
  mutate(across(c(VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc), as.numeric)) |> #converting chrtr to #numeric in order to add and get mean
  mutate(mean_moist = (rowSums(across(c(VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc))))/3) |> #calc mean
  select(treatment, date, Block, mean_moist, tag_number, mean_transp) 

```

## ANOVA Analysis

Conducting a two-way anova

```{r}
aov_model <- lm(log(mean_transp) ~ treatment, data = licor_wanted_clean)

plot(aov_model, which = 2) #need to log model

anova(aov_model)

```
